review_notes: Read the whole target and the DG left-module file it imports (DG/Module/Defs.lean). I also grepped the Curved/Right, DG/Right and other homology files for the decompose-sum pattern. The proof of `leibniz_of_map_eq_zero` is character-for-character the same as the DG one, apart from the structure name and `↦` versus `=>`. The curved structure's `isHomogeneous` and `leibniz` fields have the same types as the DG ones, so a shared lemma stated only on the Leibniz hypothesis fits both. I did not check where the right-module analogues live. I did not compile the proposed lemma. The `map_decompose` duplicate is a one-term wrapper around `DirectSum.map_decompose_shift`, so I left it out as too thin to count.

findings.excerpt: conv_lhs => rw [← DirectSum.sum_support_decompose 𝒜 a, Finset.sum_smul, map_sum]
findings.problem: The proof splits an arbitrary scalar `a` into homogeneous components and applies the Leibniz rule to each. It then kills the signed term with `dM x = 0`. This is the same non-trivial argument as `IsDGLeftModule.leibniz_of_map_eq_zero` in the imported DG file, with identical `conv` lines and identical closing rewrites. Only the structure that supplies `leibniz` differs. A fix to this argument would have to be made in both files.
findings.proposed_change: In `TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/DG/Module/Defs.lean`, add a lemma that takes the Leibniz rule as a hypothesis, not a module structure. For example: `theorem dM_smul_of_map_eq_zero_of_leibniz (hleib : ∀ {p : ℤ} {a : A}, a ∈ 𝒜 p → ∀ x : M, dM (a • x) = d a • x + p.negOnePow • (a • dM x)) (a : A) {x : M} (hx : dM x = 0) : dM (a • x) = d a • x`. Proof: the existing `classical` plus `conv_lhs`/`conv_rhs` block, then `Finset.sum_congr rfl`, then `rw [hleib (SetLike.coe_mem _) x, hx, smul_zero, smul_zero, add_zero]`. It needs no homogeneity of `dM` and no `ℳ` grading. After that, `IsDGLeftModule.leibniz_of_map_eq_zero` becomes `dM_smul_of_map_eq_zero_of_leibniz (fun ha x => hM.leibniz ha x) a hx`. The curved version, with its actual hypotheses `hM : IsCurvedDGLeftModule h ℳ dM`, becomes `dM_smul_of_map_eq_zero_of_leibniz (fun ha x => hM.leibniz ha x) a hx`. Both uses are one line, and this file already imports the DG module file.
findings.benefit: The decompose-and-sum argument is stated and maintained once. The DG and curved left-module wrappers become one-liners. Anyone who adds a further Leibniz-type structure on a graded module can reuse the lemma instead of copying the `conv` block a third time.
